Hi Sarah —

Great speaking yesterday. Per our discovery, Ledgerly will be using Redwood for two main features initially: (1) generative customer response drafts (short form, ~120 tokens per request) and (2) a context-augmented summarization pipeline for support transcripts (variable context, up to ~6k tokens).

To make the CS -> Implementation handoff smoother, can you confirm the following by EOD Monday?
- Estimated monthly active users (MAU) for the pilot and expected requests per user
- Typical session length for the summarization flow (avg number of messages per session)
- Any regulatory constraints on context storage or prefix caching

We attached a quick CSV template to drop your initial token/volume estimates. Once we have that, Monica and Grace will finalize a short model playbook (3 model candidates with cost/latency tradeoffs and recommended quantization profiles) and propose a 90-day token commitment that maps to Dedicated vs Hosted proposals.

Attachments: ledgerly_token_estimates_20281203.csv (CSV template)

Thanks — looking forward to the numbers.

Best,
Priya

Priya —

Thanks for the summary and the template. Quick answers below (very rough, happy to refine):
- Pilot MAU: 3,000 users; expected requests/user/day (gen drafts): 0.6 avg -> ~5,400 gen requests/mo
- Summarization: ~8 support messages/session avg; we estimate 1.2 sessions/user/month -> ~3,600 summaries/mo
- Typical summarization input length: ~3,500 tokens (after stitching); we may occasionally hit up to 6k tokens for multi-thread escalation cases
- Data retention: transcripts are stored for 90 days; we cannot persist full customer transcripts outside our VPC after retention window but ok with short-lived prefix caching for inference

I've filled the attached CSV and re-attached as ledgerly_token_estimates_20281204.csv. Let us know if you want a quick sync with our head of platform — he can join tomorrow morning PST.

—Sarah

Forwarding Sarah's numbers. Grace / Ben — please review and draft the three-candidate model playbook and a recommended 90-day token commitment. Key constraints to respect: 1) summarization avg input ~3.5k tokens, spike to 6k; 2) data retention policy prevents persistent external KV caches beyond 90 days; 3) the gen drafts are short (120 tokens).

Initial thinking (high-level):
- Candidate A (low-latency hosted): Llama-2-13B quantized (fast, cheaper per token for short gens) — good for drafts, not ideal for 6k contexts without chunking
- Candidate B (context-optimized): MPT/Redwood-Context-32k variant (or a 30B context-capable open model) — better for single-pass summarization of 6k windows with higher cost and GPU memory requirements
- Candidate C (hybrid routing): route small gens to Candidate A and heavy summaries to Candidate B; enable prefix caching for repeated user prefixes within 90-day retention window

Ask: Can you produce the following deliverables by EOD Friday (2028-12-08)?
1) model_playbook_v1.xlsx (3 candidates; per-token cost estimates; latency SLOs; suggested quantization/bsz)
2) token_commitment_proposal.txt (90-day commit bands tied to Dedicated sizing tiers)
3) a short ops note on how to handle 6k spikes (prefer chunking + fallback policy)

I'm happy to own the customer kickoff email once we have the playbook. Priya — please prep the HubSpot deal and calendar for a kickoff on Monday next week.

Thanks,
Monica Patel
Senior Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

Thanks, team — copying the deliverables inline and next steps.

Deliverables delivered (attached to this thread):
- redwood_model_playbook_v1.xlsx (sheets: summary, cost-latency, contextual-profile)
- ledgerly_token_estimates_20281204.csv (normalized volumes)
- token_commitment_proposal.txt (90-day bands and recommended Dedicated sizing)

Summary highlights:
- Recommended routing: Hybrid routing (Candidate C) — route gen drafts to qLlama-13B quantized; route summarization to Context-30B variant with 16k context setting (chunk & stitch for 6k max to keep latency under 800ms p99).
- 90-day proposal: conservative band -> 200k generated tokens/mo and 2.5M summarization input tokens/mo (maps to a 2-GPU Dedicated pool with burst headroom); this aligns with Ledgerly's pilot numbers and gives 30% buffer for early growth.
- Ops note: Implement prefix caching inside customer's VPC for commonly repeated metadata (customer ID, product tags) with TTL <= 90 days. For 6k spikes: chunk at 2.5k windows + parallel summarize + stitch with model-assisted coherence check.

Action items (owners):
- Priya: finalize HubSpot deal record and send kickoff invite (target: Mon 2028-12-10)
- Monica: send customer-facing playbook and run through model tradeoffs on kickoff call
- Ben: prepare a short perf runbook for Dedicated sizing & autoscale policy
- Grace: coordinate security note with Security & Compliance and confirm prefix caching approach is acceptable for Ledgerly's retention policy

I'll attach the playbook and token commitment proposal to HubSpot and the Drive link in related_links. If everyone agrees, Monica, please send the customer kickoff email today.

—Grace
